subject: GLA Roadshow — lead credit breakdown and proposed adjustments
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-29T09:14:00Z
Subject: GLA Roadshow — initial lead credit calc

Team,

Attached is my first pass at the lead-credit breakdown for the Glasgow roadshow. Quick summary up front: 124 total new leads captured; 42 leads mapped to Highland target accounts; our initial pipeline influenced shows $1.1M ARR in early-stage opps. However, I flagged 18 leads where EventPros badge scans show duplicates or missing session tags — those are the ones causing the biggest variance versus Highland's internal list.

Please review the attached sheet (Highland_Credit_Summary.xlsx) and the raw check-in CSV (event_checkin_export.csv) — I pulled the export from the kiosk vendor. Key asks:
- Marcus: sanity-check the lead->contact mapping (I used email match + company heuristic).
- Karthik: can you reconcile the 18 badge-ID mismatches with the CRM? Might be mapping to existing contacts.
- Evelyn: can you draft a short note for Highland explaining that we found scanning gaps and propose crediting method?

I also included the Drive link to the GLA KPI deck with session-level counts.

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Field Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Highland_Credit_Summary.xlsx (spreadsheet), event_checkin_export.csv (csv)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: GLA Roadshow — initial lead credit calc

On Wed, Jul 29, 2026 at 09:14, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team,
>
> Attached is my first pass...

I pulled a quick join between the check-in CSV and HubSpot exports. A few notes:
- Email matches resolve ~88% of rows; the remaining 12% are either scanner-only badge IDs or free-text company names (typos).
- Of the 18 flagged, 10 appear to be existing contacts in HS with different company variants (e.g., "Highland Capital" vs "Highland Capital LLP"). I added a "mapping_notes" column in the sheet.
- The $1.1M ARR number looks defensible for influenced opps but only ~$420k meets our 90-day sales-accepted-opportunity filter. We should be explicit about which pipeline buckets we report.

I recommend: 1) share the mapping notes with Highland, 2) propose a credit schedule that splits disputed leads 50/50 unless Highland can show stronger ownership (meeting notes, calendar invites).

Marcus
Field Ops Lead

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Emma Parsons <emma@highlandcap.com>

Date: 2026-07-30T08:22:00Z
Subject: Fwd: GLA Roadshow — lead credit breakdown and proposed adjustments

Emma — forwarding our internal read + the attachments. Short version: we captured 124 leads and mapped 42 to Highland target accounts. There are 18 leads where our kiosk data and HubSpot mapping disagree — most are typos or badge-scan duplicates. Marcus suggests a provisional 50/50 split on disputed leads and to classify pipeline numbers by SAO vs influenced.

I've attached: Highland_Credit_Summary.xlsx (with mapping notes) and event_checkin_export.csv (raw). Can you confirm Highland's preferred approach so we can finalize credits and the invoicing adjustment?

Proposed options:
- Option A: 50/50 split on the 18 disputed leads (quick, precedent-based)
- Option B: Highland provides notes/evidence for up-to-50% of disputed leads to claim full credit; we adjudicate the remainder 50/50

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if that helps.

Best,
Olga
Senior Field Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: GLA Roadshow — lead credit breakdown and proposed adjustments

Thanks Olga — appreciate the quick follow-up and the files. A few items from Highland's side:
- Our CRM shows 28 Highland-target leads from Glasgow, not 42. We pulled this with our event tag and sales follow-up list.
- About the 18 disputed: several of those contacts attended our private roundtable hosted in the afternoon (we have sign-in sheets and calendar invites) — if those map to Highland accounts they should be credited to us.
- We also noticed a cluster of badge IDs that EventPros labeled as "vendor" during morning check-in; that may be why some attendees are missing the Highland tag.

Can EventPros run a filtered badge-report (session-level) and include manual sign-in sheets? Ops @ EventPros, can you confirm what happened with the morning scanner labeling?

Emma Parsons
Head of Events, Highland Capital
emma@highlandcap.com

Hi all,

Apologies — we had a morning scanner configuration issue on the main kiosk where the operator selected the wrong badge-profile. That caused ~22 check-ins to be tagged as "vendor/partner" instead of the exhibitor session. We've extracted a corrected session-level CSV and attached it here (event_checkin_export_fixed.csv). We also scanned the paper sign-in for the Highland roundtable and attached images in the Drive link.

Next steps from our side:
- We've re-exported the full session-level file and included original badge IDs + corrected session tags.
- We recommend Redwood / Highland re-run joins on the fixed CSV; we can also send us the HubSpot export if you'd like us to do an assisted reconciliation.

Regards,
Clare D.
Operations Manager, EventPros UK
ops@eventpros.co.uk

Date: 2026-08-02T16:28:00Z
Subject: Re: GLA Roadshow — lead credit breakdown and proposed adjustments

Thanks Clare — and thanks Emma for the context.

We re-ran the mapping with EventPros' corrected CSV. Results: 14 of the 18 disputed leads now map clearly to Highland-owned contacts (sign-in + calendar evidence checks out). That leaves 4 disputed leads that remain ambiguous (partial names / multiple company variants). Per our proposed policy we recommend:
- Credit Highland for the 14 confirmed leads.
- Split the 4 ambiguous leads 50/50 (2 credits to Highland, 2 remain with Redwood).
- Adjust the invoicing credit: total creditable pipeline reduces the disputed portion from $1.1M influenced to $980k influenced and $370k qualifying SAO (numbers in attached Highland_Credit_Summary.xlsx, final sheet tab "AdjustedCredits").

If Highland agrees, we will issue a revised credit note and update the HubSpot deal record (HC-2026-07-GLA-1) to reflect the new influence totals. Emma — would you like us to prepare the credit note draft or do you want to run it from your side?

I'll prepare a short one-page summary for leadership recap and put the final numbers in the Drive deck.

Olga
Senior Field Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Highland_Credit_Summary.xlsx (finalized)
